use: Said on a bad phone or video call; the answer is kikoeru yo or kikoenai.

example.ja: もしもし？聞こえる？電波悪いみたい。
example.english: Hello? Can you hear me? The signal seems bad.

examplePolite.romaji: moshimoshi, kikoemasu ka? koe ga tooi desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: もしもし、聞こえますか？声が遠いですね。
examplePolite.english: Hello, can you hear me? You sound far away.

notes: Kikoeru means can be heard, so the sound takes ga: koe ga kikoeru. It also asks did you hear that? about a noise.

use: The standard text or call when meeting up; answer with a place + da yo, or ima mukatteru.

example.romaji: ima doko? mou eki ni tsuita yo.
example.ja: 今どこ？もう駅に着いたよ。
example.english: Where are you? I'm already at the station.

examplePolite.romaji: ima doko desu ka? kaisatsu no mae ni imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 今どこですか？改札の前にいます。
examplePolite.english: Where are you now? I'm in front of the ticket gates.

notes: To someone senior, ima dochira desu ka sounds more polite.

english: sorry to keep you waiting; here I am
use: Said when you reach a friend who has been waiting, even a minute; they often answer zenzen (not at all).

example.ja: ごめん、お待たせ！行こうか。
example.english: Sorry to keep you waiting! Shall we go?

examplePolite.romaji: omatase shimashita. sumimasen, densha ga okurete.
examplePolite.ja: お待たせしました。すみません、電車が遅れて。
examplePolite.english: Sorry to keep you waiting. My train was late.

notes: Also said when handing over something people were waiting for, like food you cooked.

use: Said when you can't talk right now; usually with ne.

example.romaji: gomen, ima densha. ato de kakenaosu ne.
example.ja: ごめん、今電車。後でかけ直すね。
example.english: Sorry, I'm on the train. I'll call you back later.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, ima te ga hanasenai node, ato de kakenaoshimasu.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、今手が離せないので、後でかけ直します。
examplePolite.english: Sorry, I'm tied up right now, so I'll call you back later.

notes: Kakenaosu means call again; kakeru alone means make a call.

use: Texted or said when someone asks where you are; add a place + ni to say where you're heading.

example.romaji: ima mukatteru! juppun gurai de tsuku.
example.ja: 今向かってる！10分ぐらいで着く。
example.english: I'm on my way! I'll be there in about ten minutes.

examplePolite.romaji: ima eki ni mukatte imasu. sugu tsukimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 今駅に向かっています。すぐ着きます。
examplePolite.english: I'm heading to the station now. I'll be there soon.

notes: Mukau means head toward. Ima iku is closer to I'm coming right now.

use: Texted or said when you reach the meeting place; add where: eki ni tsuita yo.

example.romaji: tsuita yo. kitaguchi no mae ni iru.
example.ja: 着いたよ。北口の前にいる。
example.english: I'm here. I'm in front of the north exit.

examplePolite.romaji: ima tsukimashita. iriguchi no mae ni imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 今着きました。入口の前にいます。
examplePolite.english: I just got here. I'm in front of the entrance.

notes: Past tense because you've already arrived. Mou tsuita? means are you there yet?

english: I'll be waiting; I'll wait for you
use: Said to someone on their way, or warmly at a goodbye to mean see you then.

example.romaji: wakatta. jaa, kafe de matteru ne.
example.ja: わかった。じゃあ、カフェで待ってるね。
example.english: Okay. I'll wait for you at the café, then.

examplePolite.romaji: wakarimashita. robii de matte imasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: わかりました。ロビーで待っていますね。
examplePolite.english: Understood. I'll be waiting in the lobby.

notes: To customers or seniors, omachi shite imasu is the humble version.

english: I'll be in touch; I'll get back to you
use: Said when ending a chat or call without a fixed plan; it can also be a soft no to an invitation.

example.romaji: jaa, yotei ga wakattara mata renraku suru ne.
example.ja: じゃあ、予定がわかったらまた連絡するね。
example.english: Okay, I'll get back to you once I know my plans.

examplePolite.ja: 確認して、また連絡します。
examplePolite.english: I'll check and get back to you.

notes: Renraku means contact; renraku shite means get in touch with me.

english: who is this?; may I ask who's calling?
use: Asked politely on the phone or at the door when the person is unknown; answer with your name + desu.

example.romaji: shitsurei desu ga, dochira-sama desu ka?
example.ja: 失礼ですが、どちら様ですか？
example.english: Excuse me, but may I ask who's calling?

notes: The casual dare? sounds blunt to a stranger. Business calls often use dochira-sama deshou ka.

use: Said to friends or family when you can't talk now or want to talk later, often with ne.

example.romaji: ima isogashii kara, ato de denwa suru ne.
example.ja: 今忙しいから、後で電話するね。
example.english: I'm busy now, so I'll call you later.

examplePolite.romaji: kaigi no ato de denwa shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 会議の後で電話します。
examplePolite.english: I'll call you after the meeting.

notes: To a client or senior, ato de odenwa shimasu is the humble version.

use: Said as you arrive late; the usual answer is ii yo or daijoubu.

example.romaji: okurete gomen! densha ga tomatteta n da.
example.ja: 遅れてごめん！電車が止まってたんだ。
example.english: Sorry I'm late! The train was stopped.

examplePolite.romaji: okurete sumimasen. michi ni mayotte shimaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 遅れてすみません。道に迷ってしまいました。
examplePolite.english: Sorry I'm late. I got lost.

notes: At work, okurete moushiwake arimasen is the stronger apology.

src: 折り返しお電話します
ja: 折り返しお電話します
kana: おりかえしおでんわします
english: I'll call you back; we'll return your call
use: Business phrase: staff say it when the person you want is out, and you can use it at work too.

example.romaji: tantousha ga modorimashitara, orikaeshi odenwa shimasu.
example.ja: 担当者が戻りましたら、折り返しお電話します。
example.english: When the person in charge is back, we'll call you back.

notes: Casual: orikaesu ne. Orikaeshi denwa kudasai means please call me back.

use: Texted or said before you arrive, usually with gomen and how long.

example.ja: ごめん、ちょっと遅れる。10分ぐらい。
example.english: Sorry, I'll be a bit late. About ten minutes.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, densha ga okurete ite, sukoshi okuremasu.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、電車が遅れていて、少し遅れます。
examplePolite.english: Sorry, my train's delayed, so I'll be a little late.

notes: Okureru is also used for trains: densha ga okureteru (the train's late).
